audit_findings.title: FY2025 anchor includes only five months of Encino
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $425 million pro forma net-income uplift ($5,405 million versus $4,980 million reported) and $58 million acquisition-related costs; owner-earnings impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The DCF applies a partial-year OE anchor to post-acquisition shares and cash, while acquisition-only expenses also reduce the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: The financial results of Encino have been included in EOG's consolidated financial statements beginning August 1, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter and normalization error. The filed pro forma net-income uplift equals 8.7% of the $4,886.4 million OE anchor, large enough to affect a valuation whose base value is $138.37 versus a $145.417 market price. Pro forma net income is not owner earnings, so the valuation effect cannot be quantified directly.
audit_findings.action: Construct full-year pro forma Encino owner earnings using filed pro forma results and underlying cash-flow data; remove the $58 million of genuine acquisition-only costs, include recurring operating and maintenance capital, and rerun all scenarios on the post-acquisition perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition debt interest is not at its full run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: computed $72 million pretax run-rate gap ($393 million expected 2026 senior-note interest less $321 million 2025 interest incurred), approximately $56 million after the filed 22% tax rate and about $1.48 per share in the base case
audit_findings.mechanism: A full-year recurring interest adjustment reduces equity-level OE; debt principal remains context-only and is not deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2026, EOG has no senior notes maturing and EOG expects to pay interest of $393 million on senior notes.
audit_findings.explanation: The incomplete 2025 interest burden is demonstrated, but its scale is about 1.5% of the OE anchor. Applying the model's base operating-value multiple to the approximately $56 million after-tax gap reduces base value by about $1.48 per share and bull value by about $1.66, leaving the base below market and the bull above market. It therefore does not change the valuation conclusion on the filed numbers.
audit_findings.action: Normalize OE to the $393 million annual senior-note cash interest burden, include capitalized interest attributable to the financing, remove the $6.5 million acquisition financing commitment cost, and confirm the rerun produces an adjustment near the computed scale.

audit_findings.title: Maintenance capital may understate reserve-replacement economics
audit_findings.mechanism: Any shortfall between the maintenance-capital deduction and spending required to sustain economic production directly overstates OE and compounds through forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The rate of production from crude oil and natural gas properties generally declines as reserves are produced.
audit_findings.explanation: Reserve depletion is demonstrated, but the record does not disclose the maintenance-capital amount embedded in the $4,886.4 million anchor or establish the capital required to hold production economically flat. Filed total capital expenditures and future development costs mix maintenance, growth, exploration and acquisition activity, so they cannot quantify a shortfall. Materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the anchor's maintenance-capital calculation and reconcile it to basin-level decline curves, flat-production drilling and completion requirements, recurring infrastructure, PUD conversion and leasehold replacement; rerun each scenario for the validated shortfall.

audit_findings.title: Asset-retirement cash claims may fall outside both OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $1,607 million ARO at June 30, 2026, $75 million of 2025 settlements, and $2,436 million of future abandonment costs for proved reserves; $1,607 million equals about $3.02 per share and 2.2% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Uncaptured plugging and abandonment cash payments would reduce OE or require a separate bridge deduction, but the same obligation must not be charged twice.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash requirements to settle the liability for EOG's pension and postretirement benefit obligations and the liability for dismantlement, abandonment and asset retirement obligations (see Notes 7 and 15, respectively, to Consolidated Financial Statements) are excluded because they are subject to estimates and the timing of settlement is unknown.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether maintenance capital already captures these payments is unresolved, but the filed scale is not conclusion-changing. Even mechanically subtracting the entire $2,436 million undiscounted proved-reserve abandonment estimate would reduce value by about $4.58 per share, leaving base value below market and bull value above market. Actual 2025 settlements were $75 million, only 1.5% of the OE anchor.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $75 million of 2025 and $40 million of first-half 2026 settlements through the OE calculation, reconcile the maintenance allowance to the ARO roll-forward and $2,436 million abandonment forecast, and add a bridge adjustment only for obligations not already captured.

audit_findings.title: Disposed Midland earnings may remain in the anchor alongside sale proceeds
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $165 million gross sale price and 4 MBbld production; the production was 0.77% of FY2025 crude-oil output, while $165 million equals about $0.31 per share and 0.22% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining the disposed assets' recurring OE while including their sale proceeds in cash counts value from both the operations and their disposition.
audit_findings.evidence: In January 2026, EOG signed a purchase and sale agreement for the sale of its entire interest and related fixed assets in the northern Midland Basin for $165 million, subject to customary closing adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: The post-sale perimeter inconsistency is demonstrated, although the exact recurring OE contribution is not filed. Its scale is small: the assets supplied less than 1% of 2025 crude-oil production, and even the entire gross sale price is only 0.22% of base equity value. This cannot reasonably change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Use the closing statement and property-level production and cost records to remove the northern Midland assets' recurring OE, verify the net proceeds included in June 2026 cash, and rerun the bridge and anchor without double counting.
